diagnostic_evidence.quote: check whether the estimated standard deviation is approximately zero

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims the learned std of u|a measures uncertainty and hence the predictive quality of the learned model. In the noise-free setting the target is a Dirac, so the std is expected to be about zero by design and is used only as a diagnostic. Table 1 shows MSTD of 1e-7 to 1e-5 against MRLE of 2e-3 to 5e-3, so the std is orders of magnitude below the actual error. It also does not track accuracy: M=256 has a lower MRLE than M=64 but a roughly 24 times larger MSTD. Nothing in the paper shows the std reflects model (epistemic) error. What is shown is that it recovers the magnitude of additive data noise, which is aleatoric.

failure_location.quote: provides an informative quantification of the uncertainty and hence the predictive quality of the laerned model

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to data-noise (aleatoric) uncertainty. State that in the noise-free setting the std is only a consistency diagnostic and does not bound the prediction error.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised uncertainty-quantification benefit is established only for recovering injected data noise, not for assessing the reliability of the learned operator. Any reading of the std as a confidence measure for prediction error is unsupported.
issues.title: Claim that the learned std quantifies predictive quality of the model is contradicted by the paper's own noise-free results
issues.why_classification: The repair is a rewording, but it withdraws a headline advantage (std as an indicator of predictive quality). No proof architecture changes and the noise-recovery results survive, so the loss is limited.

issues.failure_explanation: L_0 is defined as the expected value of -log q_theta(u_0|u_1,a), a Gaussian log-density. With bar-alpha_0 = 1 (empty product), the noise-free covariance choice gives Sigma_theta(1,.,.) = 0. Then q_theta(u_0|u_1,a) is a Dirac, and -log q_theta equals +infinity unless u_0 equals the mean exactly. So L_0, and hence -VLB, is infinite. The 'pre-factor' 1/(2 Sigma) that is dropped to obtain the squared-error form is infinite, so the displayed L_0 is not a consequence of the VLB. It is only an ad hoc surrogate, and the same degeneracy affects the t=1 entropy term in the appendix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat t=1 explicitly: use a small positive variance or a discrete or fixed-variance decoder for L_0, or declare the t=1 term a surrogate and drop the VLB claim for it. The training objective is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the final loss is derived from a bound on the conditional likelihood fails at t=1 for noise-free data. The training loss itself can still be used heuristically.
issues.title: L_0 term is degenerate (zero reverse variance at t=1) in the noise-free case, so the 'ignore the pre-factor' derivation is invalid
issues.why_classification: A local fix of a degenerate boundary case (t=1) suffices. The loss, algorithm and results are unchanged, and only the stated justification of one term changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The 'mean standard deviation' divides the norm of the sample std by N_s. For a fixed per-sample spread this shrinks like 1/N_s, so it measures neither the std nor the standard error (which would scale like 1/sqrt(N_s)). Reported MSTD values therefore depend on an arbitrary sample count. For noise-free tests (Tests 2-4) the stated protocol uses N_s=1, where the std of a single sample is zero or undefined. Yet Tables 1-3 report nonzero MSTD values, with the number of samples used for them left unspecified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define MSTD without the 1/N_s factor, or with a clearly justified normalisation. State the N_s used for the MSTD runs, which must be at least 2, and recompute the tables.
issues.overall_effect: The MSTD columns, and the uncertainty-recovery claims that rely on them, cannot be interpreted as standard deviations or compared across N_s.
issues.title: MSTD metric is divided by N_s and is incompatible with the stated single-sample noise-free protocol
issues.why_classification: A definitional correction plus recomputation of diagnostics is routine. The method and the main accuracy (MRLE) conclusions are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A similar result holds in the case of data perturbed by an additive
obtained from corrupting the output $u$ by an additive Gaussian noise $\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma(a))$
the true reverse distribution $p(u_{t-1} | u_t)$ has a covariance $\beta_t \mathbf{I}$

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is offered as the noisy-data analogue that justifies Sigma_theta = beta_t I for noisy data. It assumes Cov(u_0)=I. The paper's noisy data have covariance Sigma(a), and the experiments use sigma^2 I with sigma between 5e-4 and 5e-2, far from I. For Cov(u_0)=sigma^2 I, the true reverse variance is beta_t C_{t-1}/(alpha_t C_{t-1}+beta_t) with C_{t-1}=bar-alpha_{t-1} sigma^2 + 1 - bar-alpha_{t-1}. This equals beta_t only when C_{t-1}=1, and tends to the noise-free value tilde-beta_t as sigma goes to 0. So 'integrating out u_0 gives covariance beta_t I' and the optimality claim hold only for unit covariance. The proof also justifies equal entropies by a maximum-entropy property that gives only an upper bound, and its covariance recursion has beta_t and 1-beta_t swapped. Both are harmless under the identity assumption.

failure_location.quote: follows a (nonzero mean) Gaussian distribution with the identity covariance

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove the result for Cov(u_0)=sigma^2 I (or general Sigma), giving the reverse variance beta_t C_{t-1}/(alpha_t C_{t-1}+beta_t). Then either use that variance for noisy data or restrict the optimality claim to unit covariance and present beta_t as a heuristic choice.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical justification of the noisy-data covariance choice in the covariance-parameterization equation (cov) is not established for the noise levels actually used. The noise-free justification (prop:added-1) is unaffected.
issues.title: Optimality of Sigma=beta_t I for Gaussian-noise data is proved only for identity data covariance
issues.why_classification: A contained new calculation (Gaussian conditioning with general covariance) fixes the statement. It may change the covariance recommendation for noisy data, but the rest of the method and the experiments stand.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed chain only equates E_{q_theta}[-log q_theta] (the entropy of q_theta) with E_p[-log p] (the entropy of p). These agree whenever the Gaussian reverse covariances match, because Gaussian entropy depends only on the covariance. This says nothing about the data likelihood E_p[-log q_theta], which also depends on the learned means eps_theta. Achieving that likelihood would require q_theta=p, which is not shown. Further, H_{q_theta}(u_T)=H_p(u_T) holds only approximately, since p(u_T) is only approximately N(0,I). The step is also unjustified for noisy data (see ISSUE-004).

failure_location.quote: the learned parametric model $q_{\theta}$ achieves the exact likelihood under the true model $p$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by the supported statement that the chosen covariances reproduce the conditional entropies H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t) of the true reverse chain, with equality at u_T only approximately. Drop the exact-likelihood conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix conclusion that the model attains the exact likelihood is unsupported. Only covariance (entropy) matching is shown.
issues.title: Equality of entropies is claimed to give 'exact likelihood' of the learned model
issues.why_classification: Repair is a limited weakening of a side claim in the appendix. It leaves a recognizably weaker but correct statement and does not touch the main method or experiments.
